name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
authority: Ministry of MSME · implemented by KVIC, KVIBs & DICs

benefit.headline: 15–35% margin-money subsidy on a bank loan for setting up a new unit
benefit.maxValueNote: 35% (special category, rural area) on the ₹50 lakh manufacturing project ceiling
details: Project cost ceiling: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing, ₹20 lakh for business/services
Subsidy: general category 15% (urban) / 25% (rural); SC/ST/OBC/minority/women/ex-serviceman/transgender/divyang/NER/aspirational-district 25% (urban) / 35% (rural)
Own contribution just 10% (general) or 5% (special category); the rest is bank-financed
Successful units can take a 2nd upgradation loan: up to ₹1 crore (manufacturing) / ₹25 lakh (services) with 15% subsidy (20% in NER & hill states)

all.label: Brand-new unit — PMEGP funds only new projects, not existing businesses
Eligible applicant: individual (18+), SHG, registered society, production co-operative or charitable trust — companies & partnership firms are not eligible
Manufacturing or service activity — pure trading/retail is not eligible

softChecks: Applicant must be at least 18 years old
Minimum 8th-pass for manufacturing projects above ₹10 lakh and service projects above ₹5 lakh
Unit must not have availed subsidy under any other central/state self-employment scheme (incl. PMRY)
Activity must not be on the PMEGP negative list
10-day EDP training is mandatory before margin money release (projects above ₹5 lakh)
documents: Project report / DPR (the e-portal has a free generator)
Rural-area certificate (for the rural subsidy rate)
applySteps: Fill the online application on the PMEGP e-portal (kviconline.gov.in) and note your application ID
Upload documents and choose your financing bank
Appear for the district-level task force scrutiny/interview when called
On approval the file moves to your bank for sanction
Complete EDP training; margin money is credited to the loan account

name: Chief Minister Employment Generation Programme, Maharashtra
authority: Govt. of Maharashtra · DICs (urban) & MSKVIB (rural)

benefit.headline: Maharashtra's own PMEGP: 15–35% margin-money subsidy for new units
benefit.maxValueNote: 35% (special category, rural area) on the ₹50 lakh manufacturing project ceiling
details: Project cost ceiling: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing, ₹10 lakh for services
Subsidy: general 15% (urban) / 25% (rural); SC/ST/OBC/women/ex-serviceman/divyang 25% (urban) / 35% (rural)
Own contribution 10% (general) or 5% (special category)
Stackable strategy: if you miss PMEGP allocation, CMEGP is the state-funded parallel track (you can avail only one)

all.label: Business located in Maharashtra (applicant must be a Maharashtra resident)
Brand-new unit — CMEGP funds only new projects
Individual applicant (proprietorship or about-to-register individual)
Manufacturing or service activity — pure trading is not eligible

softChecks: Age 18–45 years (relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST/women/ex-servicemen/divyang)
Minimum 7th-pass for projects above ₹10 lakh; 10th-pass above ₹25 lakh
Only one person per family can avail the scheme
Must not have taken subsidy under any other government self-employment scheme
Maharashtra domicile certificate required
applySteps: Apply online at maha-cmegp.gov.in with documents
District task force scrutinises and recommends to the bank
Bank sanctions the loan; complete the mandated EDP training
Margin money subsidy is released to the loan account

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro & Small Enterprises
authority: CGTMSE Trust · Ministry of MSME + SIDBI

benefit.headline: Collateral-free loans up to ₹10 crore — the Trust guarantees your lender instead
benefit.maxValueNote: guarantee cover, not a cash subsidy — enables the loan rather than paying you
details: Guarantee ceiling raised from ₹5 crore to ₹10 crore for guarantees approved on/after 1 April 2025 (Budget 2025-26)
Cover: 85% for micro loans up to ₹5 lakh and for SC/ST/NER units; up to 90% for women-owned units; 75% standard
Annual guarantee fee rationalised: from 0.37% p.a. (loans up to ₹10 lakh)
Works on term loans and working capital from scheduled banks and member NBFCs

all.label: Micro or small enterprise (medium enterprises are outside CGTMSE)
Udyam Registration — lenders require a valid Udyam number for guarantee cover

softChecks: Loan must be from a CGTMSE member lending institution (most scheduled banks & large NBFCs)
Account must be standard (not NPA) when the guarantee is approved
Retail trade is covered with reduced guarantee parameters — confirm specifics with your lender
documents: Loan application with project report / financials
Quotations / invoices for assets being financed
applySteps: Apply for a business loan at any CGTMSE member bank/NBFC
Ask the lender to cover the facility under CGTMSE instead of demanding collateral
Lender obtains guarantee cover on the CGTMSE portal after sanction
Annual guarantee fee is charged through the lender
notes: The ₹5cr→₹10cr enhancement was verified against CGTMSE Circular No. 250/2024-25 (18 March 2025).

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (incl. Tarun Plus)
authority: MUDRA Ltd · Dept. of Financial Services, via banks/NBFCs/MFIs

benefit.headline: Collateral-free business loans up to ₹20 lakh for micro units
benefit.maxValueNote: loan facility, not a cash subsidy
details: Shishu: up to ₹50,000 · Kishore: ₹50,000–₹5 lakh · Tarun: ₹5–10 lakh
Tarun Plus (from Oct 2024): ₹10–20 lakh for borrowers who repaid a Tarun loan
Guarantee cover through CGFMU — no collateral demanded
Covers manufacturing, processing, trading, services and allied-agriculture activities

all.label: Micro enterprise — MUDRA funds non-corporate micro units
Non-corporate borrower (individual/proprietorship/partnership/SHG) — companies & LLPs are outside the MUDRA segment

softChecks: Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
Tarun Plus tier requires a successfully repaid earlier Tarun loan
Income-generating non-farm activity (allied agri like dairy/poultry/fishery is eligible)
documents: Bank statements (6 months) for existing units
Simple business plan for higher tiers
applySteps: Apply at any bank/NBFC/MFI branch or via the udyamimitra.in / JanSamarth portal
Choose the tier (Shishu/Kishore/Tarun/Tarun Plus) matching your need
Lender appraises and sanctions — no collateral, CGFMU guarantee applies
MUDRA card (working capital) issued where applicable

name: Stand-Up India
authority: Dept. of Financial Services · SIDBI · all scheduled commercial bank branches

benefit.headline: ₹10 lakh – ₹1 crore composite loan for SC/ST and women founders of new enterprises
benefit.maxValueNote: composite loan (term + working capital), not a cash subsidy
details: Composite loan covering up to ~85% of project cost (term loan + working capital)
Every bank branch is mandated to fund at least one SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur
Margin money can be reduced to ~10% by converging with other subsidy schemes (up to 25% support)
Covers manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied activities

all.label: Owner is SC/ST and/or a woman — Stand-Up India's target group
Greenfield (first-time) enterprise — existing units are not eligible

softChecks: Applicant must be 18 or older
For companies/partnerships: at least 51% shareholding & control with the SC/ST or woman entrepreneur
Borrower must not be in default to any bank or financial institution
documents: Aadhaar, PAN and caste certificate (for SC/ST applicants)
Entity documents (partnership deed / incorporation) if not individual
applySteps: Register on standupmitra.in (handholding support available) or apply directly at a bank branch / JanSamarth
Portal connects you to your chosen branch with your project profile
Bank appraises and sanctions the composite loan
Avail margin-money convergence with eligible subsidy schemes where applicable

name: PM Vishwakarma
authority: Ministry of MSME (with Skill Development & Financial Services)

benefit.headline: ₹15,000 toolkit + skill training + ₹3 lakh credit at 5% for traditional artisans
benefit.maxValueNote: toolkit e-voucher grant; the ₹3 lakh concessional credit is additional
details: ₹15,000 toolkit incentive as an e-voucher on completing basic training
Collateral-free credit: ₹1 lakh first tranche (18 months) + ₹2 lakh second tranche (30 months)
Effective interest just 5% — Government bears 8% subvention + credit guarantee
Training stipend ₹500/day; PM Vishwakarma certificate & ID; digital-transaction and marketing incentives

all.label: Artisan/craftsperson working in one of the 18 covered family-based traditional trades (carpenter, blacksmith, potter, tailor, cobbler, goldsmith…)
Self-employed individual artisan (own-account worker)
Already engaged in the trade at the time of registration

softChecks: Age 18+; only one member per family can enrol
Must not have taken PMEGP/PM SVANidhi/MUDRA loans in the last 5 years
Government/family-of-government-servant members are not eligible
Registration is via CSC with Aadhaar biometric verification
documents: Aadhaar (with linked mobile) and bank account details
Ration card (or family member Aadhaars where unavailable)
Caste/trade details as self-declared at CSC verification
applySteps: Register at the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar
Three-step verification: gram panchayat/ULB → district committee → screening committee
Complete 5-7 day basic training; claim the ₹15,000 toolkit e-voucher
Apply for the ₹1 lakh first credit tranche through the portal/bank

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
authority: Ministry of Food Processing Industries + state nodal agencies

benefit.headline: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (up to ₹10 lakh) for micro food businesses
benefit.maxValueNote: 35% of eligible project cost, capped at ₹10 lakh per unit
details: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy on project cost, max ₹10 lakh, for new and existing micro food processing units
Seed capital ₹40,000 per SHG member engaged in food processing (via SHG federation)
35% grant for common infrastructure & 50% for branding/marketing to groups (FPOs/SHGs/co-ops)
Free handholding: DPR preparation, licensing (FSSAI), training support

all.label: Food processing activity (incl. dairy, pickles, papad, bakery, oil, spice, fishery & allied products)
Micro enterprise — the scheme targets micro food processing units
Individual / proprietorship / partnership / SHG / co-operative / FPO applicants

softChecks: Scheme window verified as extended till September 2026; a 5-year extension with revised norms is under ministry proposal — apply early
Applicant should be 18+ with at least one unit per family receiving support
Bank loan is mandatory — the subsidy is credit-linked
ODOP (One District One Product) units get processing preference but others are eligible
documents: Proof of enterprise (existing units) or project plan (new units)
FSSAI licence (can be obtained with scheme handholding)
applySteps: Register on the PMFME MIS portal (pmfme.mofpi.gov.in)
A District Resource Person is assigned free of cost to prepare your DPR
Application is recommended to the bank for the credit-linked loan
Subsidy is credited to a reserve account after loan disbursal (locked 3 years)
notes: Extension status beyond Sep 2026 pending — ministry has proposed 5 more years with a higher subsidy ceiling.

name: PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (restructured 2025)
authority: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs + Dept. of Financial Services

benefit.headline: Collateral-free working capital ₹15k → ₹25k → ₹50k for street vendors, extended to 2030
benefit.maxValueNote: loan ladder with interest subsidy & cashback, not a lump-sum grant
details: Restructured Aug 2025 and extended to 31 March 2030 (₹7,332 crore outlay)
Tranche ladder: ₹15,000 → ₹25,000 → ₹50,000 on timely repayment
7% interest subsidy + digital-payment cashback up to ₹1,600
UPI-linked RuPay credit card on repaying the second loan

all.label: Street vending activity (goods, food or services vended in urban areas)
Individual vendor
Micro-scale activity
Vending on or before the cut-off — new aspirants enrol via ULB identification

softChecks: Requires Certificate of Vending / Letter of Recommendation from your Urban Local Body
Urban areas (and surrounding peri-urban/rural vendors vending in urban areas)
documents: Certificate of Vending or ULB Letter of Recommendation
applySteps: Check your ULB survey status / obtain LoR on the PM SVANidhi portal
Apply online (or via CSC/banking correspondent) for the first ₹15,000 tranche
Repay on time to unlock ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 tranches
Use digital payments to earn cashback and the RuPay credit card

name: MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification
authority: Ministry of MSME · QCI (MSME Champions component)

benefit.headline: 80–100% subsidy on Zero Defect Zero Effect certification (free for women-owned units)
benefit.maxValueNote: 100% of the ₹90,000 Gold-level fee for women-owned MSMEs; 80% for other micro units
details: Certification fees: Bronze ₹10,000 · Silver ₹40,000 · Gold ₹90,000
Subsidy: micro 80% / small 60% / medium 50%; women-owned MSMEs get 100%
Extra +10% for SC/ST-owned or NER/Himalayan/LWE/island/aspirational-district units; +5% for SFURTI / MSE-CDP cluster members
₹10,000 joining reward on taking the ZED pledge (can make Bronze effectively free); certified units get lender concessions & procurement preference

all.label: Udyam-registered MSME (free registration at udyamregistration.gov.in)
Within MSME limits (revised classification, FY 2025-26)
Manufacturing activity — ZED certifies manufacturing units (services rollout is phased)

softChecks: Unit should be operational — assessment covers live production processes
Levels are Bronze → Silver → Gold on the ZED rating scale; existing quality certifications count toward parameters
documents: Enterprise profile on the ZED portal
Existing quality/environment certificates (if any) for parameter credit
applySteps: Register on zed.msme.gov.in with your Udyam number
Take the ZED pledge (claims the ₹10,000 joining reward)
Complete the Bronze self-assessment online
Book Silver/Gold assessment with accredited agencies — subsidy is applied to the fee

name: MSME Competitive (LEAN) Scheme
authority: Ministry of MSME (MSME Champions component)

benefit.headline: Government pays 90% of your LEAN consultant — you pay ~₹12,000 to start
benefit.maxValueNote: 90% of consultancy cost at the Advanced level (cap ₹2.4 lakh); Basic capped at ₹1.08 lakh
details: 90% of implementation/consultancy cost borne by Government across Basic → Intermediate → Advanced levels
Your share at Basic level: 10% (max ₹12,000 + taxes)
Extra +5% contribution for SFURTI-cluster, women/SC/ST-owned and NER units; +5% when registering through industry associations/OEMs
Trained LEAN consultants implement 5S, Kaizen, Kanban, Poka-Yoke etc. on your shopfloor

all.label: Udyam-registered MSME
Manufacturing unit — LEAN targets shopfloor productivity
Operational unit with a running shopfloor

softChecks: Commitment to implement LEAN tools with the assigned consultant for the level duration
Group/cluster mode implementation may apply in your district
documents: Basic unit profile on the LEAN portal
applySteps: Register on lean.msme.gov.in with Udyam details
Take the LEAN pledge and pay the 10% contribution for Basic level
Assigned consultant implements Basic level (~6 months); progress to Intermediate/Advanced
Government share is settled directly with the consultant

name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries
authority: Ministry of MSME · KVIC/Coir Board nodal agencies

benefit.headline: Up to ₹5 crore grant to organise traditional artisans into a modern cluster
benefit.maxValueNote: major cluster (>500 artisans); regular clusters (≤500) get up to ₹2.5 crore, heritage clusters up to ₹8 crore
details: Regular cluster (up to 500 artisans): up to ₹2.5 crore government assistance
Major cluster (500+ artisans): up to ₹5 crore; heritage clusters (1000–2500 artisans): up to ₹8 crore
Funds common facility centres, equipment, raw-material banks, skill training, design & marketing
Minimum 100 artisans per cluster (50 in hilly/NER states)

all.label: Implementing agency: NGO / co-operative / trust / producer company / Section-8 company (individual units apply as cluster members, not directly)
Traditional industry cluster: khadi, coir, village industries, handicrafts, agro-processing

softChecks: A Special Purpose Vehicle with majority artisan representation must be formed
Land availability for the common facility centre is required
Proposals route through a Technical Agency and the scheme steering committee
documents: Implementing agency registration documents & track record
Artisan census/baseline of the cluster (100+ artisans)
applySteps: Identify the artisan cluster and form/partner with an eligible implementing agency
Submit proposal on sfurti.msme.gov.in through the nodal agency
Technical agency appraisal → scheme steering committee approval
Funds released in tranches against milestones

name: Micro & Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
authority: DC-MSME, Ministry of MSME

benefit.headline: 70–90% government grant for Common Facility Centres (up to ₹18 crore)
benefit.maxValueNote: 90% of a ₹20-crore CFC project for special-category clusters; 70% standard
details: Common Facility Centres: GoI grant 70% of project cost up to ₹20 crore (90% in NER/hill states, island territories, aspirational/LWE districts, and clusters with 50%+ micro/village, women-owned or SC/ST units)
Infrastructure development: 60% grant (₹10 crore industrial estate / ₹15 crore flatted factory); 80% for special categories
Marketing hubs/exhibition centres: 60% grant up to ₹10 crore (80% for women-entrepreneur associations)
Land can be up to 25% of project cost

all.label: Applies via a cluster SPV / industry association / co-operative — not as an individual unit
Cluster of micro & small enterprises

softChecks: SPV typically needs 20+ member MSE units with user commitment
State government recommendation is part of the approval flow
Hard copies route through State Govt / MSME-DI field institutes
documents: SPV registration & member-unit list (with Udyam numbers)
applySteps: Form the cluster SPV with member MSEs
Prepare DPR and apply online at cluster.dcmsme.gov.in
Route hard copy via State Government / MSME-DI
Steering committee approval → tranche-wise grant release

name: NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme
authority: National Small Industries Corporation

benefit.headline: Sell to government without EMD, with free tenders and the L1+15% price band
benefit.maxValueNote: market-access benefit rather than a cash amount
details: Exemption from Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) in government tenders
Tender documents issued free of cost
MSEs quoting within L1+15% may supply up to 25% of the tender at the L1 price
Access to 358 items reserved for exclusive purchase from MSEs; counts toward the 25% MSE procurement mandate
New units get provisional registration (₹5 lakh monetary limit) for one year; SC/ST units register for just ₹100+GST

all.label: Udyam-registered enterprise
Micro or small enterprise (SPRS is for MSEs)
Unit has commenced production (new units under 1 year get provisional registration)

softChecks: Third-party technical inspection of the unit is part of the process
Registration fee varies by turnover and category; NER units get 20% concession
documents: Audited financials / provisional accounts for new units
List of plant & machinery and products
applySteps: Apply online at nsicspronline.com with documents
Pay the category/turnover-based fee
Technical inspection of the unit is conducted
G.P. Registration certificate issued — quote in government tenders with exemptions

name: NSIC Raw Material Assistance
authority: National Small Industries Corporation

benefit.headline: Buy raw material now, pay NSIC in up to 180 days (8.75% onward)
benefit.maxValueNote: credit facility against bank guarantee, not a subsidy
details: Finances indigenous & imported raw material purchases with up to 180 days credit
Interest from 8.75% p.a. for well-rated micro units (rates effective 01.07.2025); 9.25–10.25% for others
NSIC handles bulk procurement — better rates than buying alone
Processing fee 0.5–1% p.a.; security via bank guarantee from approved banks

all.label: Udyam-registered MSME
Manufacturing MSME needing raw-material credit
Production activity that consumes raw material
Operational unit (NSIC inspects the unit before sanction)

softChecks: Bank guarantee from an approved bank is mandatory security
Concessional rates require a timely-repayment track record; delays attract 1.25%/quarter penal interest
documents: Application form to the nearest NSIC branch
applySteps: Submit application at the nearest NSIC branch office
NSIC conducts preliminary appraisal and unit inspection
Limit sanctioned; sign agreement and furnish bank guarantee
Raw material financed with up to 180 days to repay

name: Procurement and Marketing Support Scheme
authority: DC-MSME, Ministry of MSME

benefit.headline: Government pays your stall & travel for domestic trade fairs
benefit.maxValueNote: indicative ceiling per event — exact caps depend on fair category and space
details: Reimbursement of space rent and contingency for participation in domestic trade fairs/exhibitions
Higher support rates for women/SC/ST/NER entrepreneurs
Funds vendor-development programmes, domestic capacity-building workshops
Supports adoption of GeM, e-commerce onboarding, packaging & barcode awareness

all.label: Udyam-registered enterprise
Micro or small enterprise
Operating business with products/services to exhibit

softChecks: Participation must be in MSME-approved fairs/exhibitions for that financial year
Reimbursement caps vary by event — confirm the sanctioned list with your MSME-DFO before booking
applySteps: Check the approved event calendar with your nearest MSME-DFO (Development & Facilitation Office)
Apply for participation under PMS before the event
Attend and retain all invoices
Submit the reimbursement claim through the DFO
notes: Scheme confirmed live on DC-MSME; per-event caps not re-verified — treat amounts as indicative.

name: International Cooperation Scheme
authority: Ministry of MSME

benefit.headline: Airfare + stall reimbursed for international trade fairs & delegations
benefit.maxValueNote: indicative per-event support — exact caps depend on destination and enterprise category
details: Reimburses economy airfare and space/stall rent for MSEs exhibiting abroad (higher % for women/SC/ST/NER entrepreneurs)
Capacity Building of First-Time Exporters (CBFTE) component: reimburses RCMC fees, export insurance premium and testing/certification for first-time exporters
Delegations and buyer-seller meets organised through industry associations

all.label: Udyam-registered MSME
Within MSME limits
Pursuing export/international market development
Operating business with exportable products/services

softChecks: Event participation generally routes through eligible industry associations / registered bodies
First-time exporter reimbursements (RCMC, insurance, testing) need proof of export initiation
applySteps: Register on ic.msme.gov.in
Apply for the event/component (fair, delegation, or CBFTE reimbursement) before participation
Attend / complete the export step and retain invoices
File the online reimbursement claim
notes: Scheme live; exact reimbursement caps vary by event/geography — verify the current ceiling on the IC portal before travel.

name: Public Procurement Policy benefits & MSME Samadhaan protection
authority: Ministry of MSME (statutory: MSMED Act 2006 + Procurement Policy Order 2012)

benefit.headline: 25% of central purchases reserved for MSEs — plus statutory interest on late payments
benefit.maxValueNote: statutory rights & market access rather than a cash amount
details: Minimum 25% of central ministries'/PSUs' annual procurement must come from MSEs (4% from SC/ST-owned, 3% from women-owned MSEs)
358 items reserved for exclusive procurement from MSEs
Tender-set exemption and EMD exemption for registered MSEs
MSMED Act: buyers must pay within 45 days, else compound interest at 3× RBI bank rate — file claims on MSME Samadhaan
GeM onboarding gives direct access to government buyers

all.label: Udyam Registration is the gateway to procurement preference & Samadhaan
Micro or small enterprise (procurement policy covers MSEs)
Operating business able to supply goods/services

softChecks: Register on GeM (gem.gov.in) to actually receive government orders
Samadhaan claims need invoices proving supply and the 45-day breach
applySteps: Complete Udyam Registration (free) and register as a seller on GeM
Quote in tenders with EMD/tender-fee exemptions as an MSE
For payments delayed beyond 45 days, file on samadhaan.msme.gov.in
The MSE Facilitation Council adjudicates with statutory interest

name: Maharashtra Industries, Investment & Services Policy 2025 — MSME incentives
authority: Industries Dept., Govt. of Maharashtra · DIC (for MSMEs)

benefit.headline: 30–100% of your fixed capital investment back as SGST refund over 5–10 years
benefit.maxValueNote: illustrative: a ₹3.5 crore-FCI unit in a D+ taluka at the 70% IPS cap; actual scales with investment & zone
details: Industrial Promotion Subsidy (SGST reimbursement) by taluka zone: A 30% of FCI (5 yrs) · B 40% (7 yrs) · C 50% (7 yrs) · D 60% (10 yrs) · D+ 70% (10 yrs) · Vidarbha/Marathwada belts 80% · no-industry/aspirational districts 100%
Food processing, green energy & Industry 4.0 units: +20% cap and +2 years
Stamp duty: 50% waiver (zones A/B), 100% exemption (C and beyond); electricity duty exemption 3 years (A/B) or full period (C+)
Interest subsidy up to 5% p.a. (cap ₹1 crore/yr) and power tariff subsidy ₹1/unit in C+ zones
Capital subsidy 20% of FCI (cap ₹25 crore) for thrust sectors
Replaced PSI-2019 on 31 Dec 2025; valid until 30 Dec 2030

all.label: Unit located in Maharashtra (benefit scales by taluka zone)
Manufacturing enterprise under the MSMED Act (IT/BT units also covered by the policy)
MSME unit (large/mega units have separate incentive tracks)

softChecks: Obtain the Eligibility Certificate via the Invest Maharashtra / MAITRI portal after completing one 'effective step' (land, registration or MPCB consent)
New units, expansions and diversifications all qualify; check your taluka's zone classification
Excluded: alcohol/tobacco products and textile units covered by the separate textile policy
Annual IPS claims require GSTR returns + CA certification
applySteps: Verify your taluka zone (A/B/C/D/D+/NID) with the District Industries Centre
Complete one effective step and apply for the Eligibility Certificate on the Invest Maharashtra portal
Commission the unit and commence production
File annual IPS (SGST reimbursement) claims with GSTR returns and CA certificate
notes: Policy GR dated 31 Dec 2025 (replaces PSI-2019). Zone-wise percentages verified via secondary analysis of the GR; confirm your unit's exact entitlement with the DIC before financial commitments.

name: Annasaheb Patil Mahamandal — Interest Reimbursement (IR-I/IR-II)
authority: Annasaheb Patil Arthik Magas Vikas Mahamandal, Govt. of Maharashtra

benefit.headline: Your business loan becomes near interest-free — up to ₹3 lakh interest refunded
benefit.maxValueNote: IR-I individual cap: full interest (≤12% p.a.) on loans up to ₹10 lakh, max ₹3 lakh over 5 years
details: IR-I (individual): bank loan up to ₹10 lakh — government refunds the interest (up to ₹3 lakh over max 5 years)
IR-II (group): loans up to ₹50 lakh for partnerships/FPOs — interest refund up to ₹15 lakh
Refund credited against EMI proof, making the loan effectively interest-free
Targets Maratha-community and economically backward youth not covered by caste-corporation schemes

all.label: Maharashtra permanent resident
Individual entrepreneurs (IR-I) or partnership/FPO groups (IR-II)

softChecks: Primarily for Maratha community & economically backward groups outside other corporation schemes
Family income within the non-creamy-layer limit (~₹8 lakh/yr)
Age limits apply (men up to ~50, women up to ~55); one-time benefit per person
Loan must be from a recognised bank; refund claimed against EMI receipts
documents: Aadhaar, PAN and Maharashtra domicile certificate
Project report and bank loan sanction letter
EMI payment proofs for refund claims
applySteps: Register on udyog.mahaswayam.gov.in and obtain the Letter of Intent (LOI)
Take the LOI to a recognised bank and get your business loan sanctioned
Start repaying EMIs and upload proof on the portal
Interest refund is credited periodically up to the cap

name: Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Women Startup Scheme
authority: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS)

benefit.headline: ₹1–25 lakh non-dilutive grant for women-led Maharashtra startups
benefit.maxValueNote: grant ceiling per startup; no equity taken
details: Financial assistance from ₹1 lakh up to ₹25 lakh as a grant (no equity dilution)
For women-led startups registered in Maharashtra with DPIIT recognition
Implemented by Maharashtra State Innovation Society in application rounds

all.label: Startup registered and based in Maharashtra
Woman founder holding more than 51% equity
Registered entity capable of DPIIT recognition (Pvt Ltd / LLP / registered partnership)
Operational for more than one year
Annual turnover between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore

softChecks: DPIIT startup recognition is required before applying
Applications open in rounds via MSInS — the round was closed at our last verification; watch msins.in for the next window
applySteps: Obtain DPIIT recognition for the startup (startupindia.gov.in)
Watch msins.in / the scheme application portal for the open round
Submit the online application with pitch and financials
Shortlisted startups pitch to the selection committee for the grant

name: Maharashtra Integrated & Sustainable Textile Policy 2023-28 — capital subsidy
authority: Co-operation, Marketing & Textiles Dept., Govt. of Maharashtra

benefit.headline: 30–45% capital subsidy on fixed investment for textile units (+5% special category)
benefit.maxValueNote: illustrative: 45% + 5% top-up on a ₹2 crore Zone-1 investment; policy covers units up to ₹50 crore
details: Zone-wise capital subsidy on fixed capital investment: Zone 1 — 45% · Zone 2 — 40% · Zone 3 — 35% · Zone 4 — 30%
Additional 5% for units run by SC/ST/minority/ex-servicemen/women entrepreneurs
Applies to MSME textile units (investment up to ₹50 crore): spinning, weaving, knitting, processing, garmenting & technical textiles
Separate solar-power capital subsidy guidelines for textile units under the same policy

all.label: Textile unit located in Maharashtra
Manufacturing unit in the textile value chain
MSME-scale unit (policy MSME track covers investment up to ₹50 crore)

softChecks: Unit must be in the textile value chain (ginning to garmenting/technical textiles) — non-textile manufacturers use MIISP 2025 instead
Note: textile units covered here are excluded from MIISP/PSI incentives (no double-dipping)
Zone classification of your taluka determines the percentage
applySteps: Confirm your zone and eligible activity with the Textiles Department / DIC
Apply with project details on the Mahatextile portal
Eligibility scrutiny and sanction by the department
Subsidy disbursed against verified fixed capital investment
